mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPI increases and subsequent Fed rate hikes is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE spikes and subsequent market performance is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and subsequent market performance is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and subsequent market performance is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and subsequent market performance is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in one month signals strengthening labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and subsequent market performance is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals strengthening demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and subsequent market performance is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points simultaneously, it signals a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on market performance is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
